findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. This part works.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The second section on the page is an error message. The opening promises that Athena records models, cost and verdict, and this section was meant to show that, but it shows nothing, which makes the promise harder to believe.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The site is Athena's, but almost all of the page explains the inner workings of a different tool, firstmate, in detail (12 transition cards, 45 claims). Someone who came to learn about Athena has to scroll past firstmate jargon such as yolo, captain call and close-pending to reach anything else about Athena.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and the sections States, Counters, Transitions, Why it is built this way, Glossary, Claims and sources

findings.text: Next steps are concrete and linked from the top of the page: the repository URL, a clone command, prerequisites, ./setup.sh and an example `athena ask "add a changelog"`. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: The page says Athena is written in Rust, but the prerequisites do not mention a Rust toolchain and do not say whether setup.sh installs one. A newcomer may wonder why a C linker is needed and whether anything else is.
findings.source: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm"

findings.text: This link in the header speaks to the project's owner, not to a visitor. A newcomer does not know which proposals or whose decision it means.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term is undefined. That is honest, but it leaves a reader of the firstmate study with terms they cannot pin down.
findings.source: Glossary entries for captain call, durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake: "The firstmate source does not define..."

findings.text: These passages describe how the page was produced (an earlier pass that missed paths, the internal folder layout). They mean little to a first-time visitor and make the page feel like an internal artifact.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f3: "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths..." and About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/"

findings.text: The claim links run from statement to claim to exact file lines at a pinned commit. This shows what Athena says it does, tracing every statement to a source, and a newcomer can check it.
findings.source: "Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end."
